title: Product Detail Photos: Close-Ups of Texture | AIVideosUGC
description: Turn one sharp photo into a close-up of stitching, grain, hardware, or finish. Use these product detail photos in a listing gallery and in paid ads.
h1: Product Detail Photos of Stitching, Grain and Finish
lead: Open a close-up scene, add one sharp photo of the feature, and download a square image. The same photo can also start a clip with a voice about that feature.

steps.d: Upload a steady, well-lit photo where the stitching, texture or clasp is already visible. That feature becomes the subject of the close-up.
Name one feature to enlarge and one simple setting. The result is a square image where that detail fills the picture.
Download the close-up and check color and construction against the source. Place it after the full product photo, not in its place.

faq.q: What is a product detail photo?
faq.a: A square close-up of one feature shoppers use to judge construction, such as stitching, grain, a clasp, a zipper or the finish. It comes from a sharp photo of that feature.

faq.q: How do I make product detail photos?
faq.a: Upload a steady photo where the feature is already visible, name that feature, and download a square where it fills the picture. Check it against your photo before you post.

faq.q: Why use this instead of a close-up photo shoot?
faq.a: A sharp phone photo can be the source, so you skip a separate close-up session. You still compare the color and how it is built before posting. The close-up should only show texture that was in your photo.

faq.q: Who is a detail photo for?
faq.a: Shops that need shoppers to inspect material or hardware, including bags, leather goods, jewelry, shoes, watches, apparel and furniture.
Yes. No editing experience is required. Upload the photo, name one feature, and download. A blurry wide shot will not become a readable close-up.
One feature per file. Start with the question shoppers ask, such as stitch, grain, clasp, zipper, rim or finish. Add another file only for a different feature.

faq.q: Can I upload my own photo?
faq.a: Yes. Upload your own sharp photo. If the stitch or clasp is blurry or out of the picture, take another photo. The result should only use texture from your photo.

faq.q: Where can I use the close-up?
faq.a: Use it after the full product photo in the listing gallery, and in paid ads. A clip from the same photo can go on TikTok, Instagram, Facebook, or YouTube. The download has no watermark.

No. There is no free plan. Each product photo costs 24 credits. A credit is a unit your plan spends. You see the cost before it starts, and if it fails those credits come back. Plans start at $24.50 a month.
Yes. Use the close-up in your own listings and ads. The download has no watermark. It does not replace the full product photo.

faq.q: Why start from a template close-up?
faq.a: The picture is already filled by one feature, so you do not have to build that close view from nothing. You still place the full product photo first.

faq.q: Can I add a voice, a presenter or another language?
faq.a: Yes. The same photo can start a clip with an on-screen person, a script, and a voice in another language. Paste the product link, or use the API, which is how your own shop software starts it. Then check the feature against your photo.

reviews.h2: How shops use a detail close-up
reviews.lead: One feature fills the picture, taken from a sharp photo. A voice or a presenter can point at that same feature.

items.d: A bag shop enlarges a handle stitch so the thread fills the square, then checks it against the source.
A belt shop brings the leather grain forward from a sharp photo, then makes a short clip from that same photo.
A wallet shop has an AI presenter point at a painted edge that already fills the picture.
A jewelry shop enlarges the clasp and shortens the spoken line in the built-in editor.
A shoe shop shows the sole seam and the stitching, then a voice in another language for a second market.
A watch shop enlarges the side knob and edits the script without leaving the page.
A jacket shop uses an AI presenter beside zipper teeth that fill the picture.
A home shop makes a tabletop grain close-up from a photo that already showed the surface, with no new light setup.
A hardware shop pastes the product link, enlarges a metal knob, and makes a second version.
An apparel shop types the bottom seam on this page, keeps the full garment photo first, and checks the close-up.
